title: Whitening partition across the seven breadth recovery systems (known-pose d'^2, raw vs whitened state maps)
status: All seven breadth systems' recovery d'^2 survive amplitude whitening (ratio 1.12-1.51, every one above 1), none collapsing like the pure-batch apoferritin reference (0.16) or anywhere near it. The recovery maps are amplitude-spectrum-matched between the two states at build time (build_full_maps, amplitude_match=spectrum), so the between-state amplitude/envelope channel that carries batch is removed before scoring; the whitening partition confirms the residual is phase/structural (whitening upweights the high-frequency shells and d'^2 rises). Each system's two state maps come from two independent collections (distinct cryoSPARC projects, listed per row).

provenance.code_commit_note: ribo compute snapshot SOURCE_COMMIT=6f5f462d, the same snapshot that produced recovery_fullmaps_pools/*/score_a.json; this whitening analysis run 2026-10-16.
provenance.method: Per system: experiments/realdata/score_pool.py --known-pose --calibrate poses --band-limit 0.125 --subsample 4000 --seed 0 (pool A, the arguments of recovery_fullmaps_pools/<sys>/score_a.json) against tmpl_a.mrc/tmpl_b.mrc raw, then against the maps whitened by experiments/crosssession/whiten_map.py (radial amplitude flattening, phases kept). d'^2 is result.oracle_closed_form.d2_pool; the raw value reproduces score_a.json exactly for every system.
provenance.reference: results/crosssession_null.json carries the matching SpCas9 flagship (ratio 1.16) and apoferritin pure-batch (0.16) partitions on non-amplitude-matched maps.
